sentences.text: Mr M. L. Wankhade, Advocate for Applicant.

Mr M. K. Goyanka, App for respondent/State.
 .....
 Coram : Advait M. Sethna, J.
 Date : 22 July 2025

P. C. :
1. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2.
These proceedings relate to C.R.No.0085/2025.
The FIR is lodged on 31/03/2025 at 21:35 hours with the Wadhwana Police Station, Dist. Latur.

The offences are registered under Sections 123,
223, 274, 275 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and under Section 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act.
3. The role ascribed of the present applicant in the FIR is that the alleged contraband was found in his vehicle.
4.
It appears that there are several orders passed in relation to this issue by the different Courts.

The Supreme Court has recently  952.25aba  (2)
passed an order in Special Leave to Appeal (Cri.) No.8698/2023 in the case of Eknath Bhalchandra Patil Vs. The State of Maharashtra,
Pratap Vishwambhar Bhure vs The State Of Maharashtra on 22 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140945517/
1 where the Supreme Court in its order dated 28/07/2023 has categorically observed that the Petitioner therein shall not be arrested in connection with Crime No.354/2022, subject to condition that he shall cooperate with the investigation.

sentences.text: The Supreme Court has also observed that the issue regarding applicability of Section 123 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita [Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code] is pending before the Supreme Court.
The said order (supra) has been confirmed by the Supreme Court by an order dated 11/09/2023.
5. Mr Goyanka, learned APP yet to advance his submissions in all these matters/Applications where an endeavour is being made to hear these finally.
Mr Goyanka would not dispute that the alleged contraband is seized and recovered.

Considering the facts in the present case, as also the orders passed by the Supreme Court, which are extremely recent in nature, the applicants deserve to be protected in terms of the following order :-
 ORDER (i) Until adjourned date of hearing, in the event of arrest of the applicant, in connection with C.R.
No.0085/2025, registered with Wadhwana Police Station, District Latur, for the offences punishable under Sections 123, 223, 952.25aba 274, 275 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and under Section 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act.
, the applicant is directed to be released on bail on his furnishing PR bond in the sum of Rs. 20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand Only) with one or more sureties in the like amount.
(ii) The applicant shall attend the concerned Police Station on every Monday at 11.30 am, until the further orders and shall cooperate with the investigation.
(iii) The Applicant shall furnish details of residential address and other contact details such as the mobile number etc. to the concerned police station.
If there is any change in the contact details, the same shall be immediately informed to the concerned police station.

(iv) The applicant shall not leave the jurisdiction of the competent Court without prior permission,
until further orders.
